title: Nitrogen Generation System
model_title: Nitrogen Generation System — Pressure Swing Adsorption (Carbon Molecular Sieve)

introduction.definition: A pressure-swing-adsorption (PSA) nitrogen generator makes nitrogen from compressed air. Two adsorbers filled with carbon molecular sieve take turns: at pressure the sieve takes up oxygen much faster than nitrogen, so nitrogen passes to a buffer vessel; the bed is then depressurised to release the oxygen and regenerate, while the other bed takes over.

pressure.title: Kinetic separation by pressure swing
pressure.description: Carbon molecular sieve separates by speed, not equilibrium: O₂ molecules (≈ 0.346 nm) diffuse into the pores much faster than N₂ (≈ 0.364 nm). With feed air at ≈ 7–10 bar(g) the CMS takes up O₂ in the short cycle (≈ 60 s) and N₂ passes through as product (purity typically 95 – 99.999 %). The tower is then depressurised to atmosphere, releasing the O₂-rich gas, while the other tower takes over; a pressure-equalisation step between towers saves air.

video_tutorials.title: Nitrogen Generation System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Nitrogen Generation System.
A pressure-swing-adsorption (PSA) nitrogen generator makes nitrogen from compressed air.

Two adsorbers filled with carbon molecular sieve take turns: at pressure the sieve takes up oxygen much faster than nitrogen, so nitrogen passes to a buffer vessel; the bed is then depressurised to release the oxygen and regenerate, while the other bed takes over.
Typical applications include inert blanketing and purging of tanks and vessels; food packaging, laser cutting and instrument purge.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Nitrogen Generation System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Nitrogen Generation System.
Check purity, pressure and cycle.
Change feed filters; calibrate analyser.
Service valves; check CMS.
Watch for purity drops: o₂ alarm. Common cause: leaking valve, oil-poisoned cms, overdraw.
Watch for cms dust: filter blockage. Common cause: bed movement.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
